title: Representability of every modular lattice by submodules
statement: Is every modular lattice isomorphic to the lattice of all submodules of some module over some ring?
status: As of November 2026: false. Submodule lattices are Arguesian; non-Desarguesian projective-plane lattices are modular and not Arguesian. This obstruction predates the 1973 talk \citep{jonsson1954modular,herrmanntakach2005subgroup}.

title: Classification of finite-dimensional r-subspace systems
statement: For a field \(k\) and fixed \(r\), describe all ordered systems \((V;E_1,\ldots,E_r)\) of subspaces in a finite-dimensional \(k\)-space up to simultaneous linear isomorphism, equivalently the finite-dimensional representations of \(D^r\).
status: As of November 2026: the algebraically closed-field classification is finite for at most three subspaces and tame for four; five subspaces already encode arbitrary matrix pairs. Earlier occurrences are special cases of this general problem. This is distinct from the deformation question GP-1970-23 \citep{gelfandponomarev1971quadruples,bernsteingelfandponomarev1973coxeter}.

title: The conic triple in polynomial and entire-function rings
statement: For \(c=z_1^2+z_2^2-1\), do there exist \(f_1,f_2\) in the specified function algebra such that \((z_1+cf_1,z_2+cf_2)\) generates its unit ideal? The coefficient field and function algebra are part of the question; the notebook's ``common divisor'' is an imprecise formulation.
status: As of 9 November 2026: affirmative over \(\mathbb C[z_1,z_2]\), hence for complex entire functions and the algebra of entire functions of finite exponential type, by the certificate checked in the critical appendix. Negative for real-valued continuous coefficients on the real disk. Brudnyi's later general theorem settles unrestricted entire reduction. No unresolved C/D contribution is inferred from the notebook's missing coefficient restriction.

title: Serre's problem for projective modules over a polynomial ring
statement: For a field \(k\) and finite \(n\), is every finitely generated projective \(k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)-module free? This occurrence announces the case \(n=3\) without recording its then-needed field restriction.
status: As of 9 November 2026: solved affirmatively by Quillen and Suslin in 1976. The 1974 Vaserstein--Suslin announcement proves the three-variable case for perfect fields or characteristic different from two. The statement of the general modern theorem must not erase that historical distinction.
